content.title: About
content.content: Romaine lettuce is a crisp, leaf vegetable belonging to the Asteraceae family. It features long, slightly wavy leaves with a firm, light‑green core. Raw romaine is commonly used in salads, sandwiches, and as a side because of its mild, slightly nutty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Romaine is considered one of the most nutrient‑dense lettuce varieties due to its high vitamin and mineral content.
Its name derives from the ancient Roman city of Rome, where it was cultivated in antiquity.
Leaves can grow up to 30 cm long while the core remains crunchy even after light cooking.
Romaine lettuce is the classic base for Caesar salad.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides over 100 µg of vitamin K, essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: High in vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene in the leaves converts to vitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is needed for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Low‑calorie fiber source
items.content: One cup of shredded romaine offers about 2 g of dietary fiber, aiding digestion and satiety.

items.title: Contains potassium and magnesium
items.content: These minerals help regulate blood pressure and support muscle function.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw leafy greens can harbor Salmonella or E. coli; thorough washing before consumption is recommended.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Conventional farming may leave pesticide traces; choosing organic romaine reduces this risk.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience leaf‑vegetable allergies, resulting in itching or swelling.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Romaine lettuce can be eaten raw in salads, added to sandwiches, used as the base for Caesar dressing, or lightly grilled. Before serving, rinse the leaves well and pat dry.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store romaine in the refrigerator in a bag with a slight moisture or in a container lined with a paper towel. It stays fresh for 7‑10 days when kept cold. Remove any wilted leaves to extend shelf life.
